summary: Small set of services: React (Vite SPA) (web) + Kotlin Multiplatform + Compose Multiplatform (Android + iOS) on Java 25 LTS + Spring Boot with Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL 17, hosted on AWS ECS on Fargate — ap-south-1 (Mumbai), at an estimated $1660-7684/month.

frontend.choice: React (Vite SPA) (web) + Kotlin Multiplatform + Compose Multiplatform (Android + iOS)
frontend.justification: Web: React (Vite SPA) — Rich interactive screens for a fintech product; team already writes typescript for the UI; good security (priority 5/5); good maintainability (priority 4/5). Mobile: Kotlin Multiplatform + Compose Multiplatform — Team already writes java, kotlin for the mobile app; one codebase for Android and iOS; good security (priority 5/5); good maintainability (priority 4/5).

alternatives.why_not: React fits better: Angular's learning curve is 4/5 for a senior team (team.experience=senior), against 2/5 for React: priorities.time_to_market=3 is below the 4 that would repay the extra ramp-up (close call). Known limit of Angular: upgrades are mandatory: each major is supported for a fixed window (24 months from Angular 22, made of 12 active + 12 LTS; v20 and v21 get 18 months), so the app must move to a new major at least every 18-24 months.

No priority or requirement this input states separates Vue 3 from React (priorities.cost=2, priorities.scalability=4, priorities.maintainability=4, priorities.security=5); React rates higher only on priorities this input leaves at the neutral 3 (priorities.time_to_market=3). Known limit of Vue 3: smaller hiring pool and component ecosystem than React.
With priorities.security=5, Kotlin Multiplatform + Compose Multiplatform is stronger on security (close call). Known limit of React Native: JS runtime overhead on very low-end phones.

With priorities.security=5 and priorities.scalability=4, Kotlin Multiplatform + Compose Multiplatform is stronger on security and built to scale further. Known limit of Ionic Capacitor: WebView performance on low-end devices.

tradeoffs: The first load waits for the JavaScript bundle, so page weight matters on slow devices
iOS tooling less mature than native Swift

database.choice: Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL 17 — ap-south-1 (Mumbai) (multi-AZ / zone-redundant HA)
database.justification: Strict ACID transactions for money movement and ledger postings; good security (priority 5/5); good maintainability (priority 4/5). The 99.95% target uses a standby in a second zone with automatic failover and point-in-time recovery. Automated backups and snapshots stay in India, in ap-south-1 (Mumbai); if a copy is enabled, keep it in a second Indian region such as ap-south-2 (Hyderabad), as RBI localisation requires storage only in India.

alternatives.why_not: With priorities.security=5 and priorities.maintainability=4, Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL 17 is stronger on security and easier to maintain.
With priorities.maintainability=4, Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL 17 is easier to maintain; it fits better: strict ACID transactions for money movement and ledger postings (requirements.payments=true).

tradeoffs: Vertical write scaling; sharding needs extensions

pareto.note: No eligible option rates at least as well on all six priorities (cost, delivery, scalability, performance, maintainability, security).

confidence.label: high
confidence.basis: stability 1.00 (robust) over 54 priority vectors; score margin 3.2 over the runner-up.

database.contrast: Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL 17 rather than Amazon RDS for MySQL 8.4. With priorities.security=5 and priorities.maintainability=4, Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL 17 is stronger on security and easier to maintain. Trade-off accepted: Vertical write scaling; sharding needs extensions.

hosting.choice: AWS ECS on Fargate (+ Application Load Balancer) — ap-south-1 (Mumbai)
hosting.justification: Runs across availability zones for the 99.95% target; good security (priority 5/5); good scalability (priority 4/5). Satisfies the hard constraints (cloud_preference aws, managed_cloud (no servers to patch), data_residency india -> ap-south-1 (Mumbai)).

alternatives.choice: AWS Elastic Beanstalk (managed platform on EC2)
alternatives.why_not: With priorities.security=5, AWS ECS on Fargate is stronger on security; the EC2/VM operating system stays in your patching and hardening scope for iso27001, pci_dss, rbi_localisation (compliance=dpdp,iso27001,pci_dss,rbi_localisation).

Spring Boot is a long-running JVM server: slow cold starts and per-invocation connection pools on functions (team.languages=java,kotlin,typescript); ~10,000 concurrent users would open relational connections per function instance; needs a connection proxy (scale.peak_concurrent_users=10000). Known limit of AWS Lambda + API Gateway: cold starts hurt tight p95 targets.

tradeoffs: Load balancer and NAT add fixed monthly cost
More AWS concepts (VPC, IAM, task definitions) than a PaaS

supporting.justification: ~500 GB of files in 12 months: uploads (images, documents) go straight from clients to object storage via signed URLs. Private bucket, server-generated signed URLs, encryption with managed keys.

alternatives.why_not: with ~500 GB of data expected in 12 months (scale.data_volume_gb_12_months), files inside the database bloat every backup and cost more per GB than object storage
zero egress fees, but a second vendor outside AWS

tradeoffs: Egress charges for heavy downloads

supporting.choice: Amazon ElastiCache for Valkey in ap-south-1 (Mumbai)
supporting.justification: ~10,000 concurrent users would otherwise send every lookup to the database (cache and pub/sub layer).

alternatives.why_not: 7.4-7.8 are source-available (RSALv2/SSPLv1) and Redis 8+ adds an AGPLv3 option (copyleft for network use); Valkey keeps the BSD licence
the database absorbs every hot read from ~10,000 concurrent users and there is no cross-instance pub/sub

tradeoffs: Another stateful component to size and monitor

supporting.justification: Payment-gateway webhooks and ledger postings at ~300,000 users processed idempotently with retries, so none of it blocks a request.

alternatives.why_not: a slow or failed call would lose or double-apply a payment event

tradeoffs: Consumers must be idempotent

supporting.choice: Razorpay (UPI, cards, netbanking) — RazorpayX Payouts for UPI loan disbursals to borrowers; Subscriptions with UPI AutoPay / e-mandate for recurring collections
supporting.justification: The description requires UPI. Taking payments for a fintech product (requirements.payments) through hosted checkout keeps card data off your servers, which can qualify for PCI DSS SAQ A (your acquirer confirms; protect the checkout page from script attacks). Payment confirmation is trusted only from signed server-side webhooks. For lending, disburse straight to the borrower's bank account and collect repayments directly into the lender's (regulated entity's) account — no pooled pass-through accounts (RBI Digital Lending Directions 2025). pci_dss: the gateway is PCI DSS Level 1; your scope still covers the pages that embed checkout.

alternatives.why_not: comparable Indian gateway; Razorpay chosen for combined UPI + payouts + subscriptions documentation
India accounts are invite-based and UPI coverage is narrower

tradeoffs: Per-transaction fees (~2% on domestic cards at Razorpay's standard pricing) are charged on revenue, not in the infrastructure band
Webhook handling must be idempotent

supporting.justification: At ~300,000 users, static assets (scripts, images, fonts) are cached near users so the origin serves less traffic; only non-personal files are cached, never signed-in responses.

alternatives.why_not: every asset request from the 300,000 expected users would hit the origin, adding latency and origin load

tradeoffs: Cache invalidation on deploys

supporting.choice: Separate Python inference service (FastAPI + ONNX Runtime) in the same private network
supporting.justification: The core API is Java 25 LTS + Spring Boot; a small Python service serves the model behind an internal endpoint, so model code stays in Python's ML tooling without changing the API's language. Credit-scoring outputs and their inputs are logged for audit and explainability.

alternatives.why_not: managed MLOps, but always-on endpoint cost before volume justifies it

tradeoffs: Model versioning, drift monitoring and fairness review are your responsibility

supporting.justification: Java 25 LTS + Spring Boot tests run on every push and a passing build deploys to AWS ECS on Fargate; the cost band reserves $0-20/month for a team of 8 (planning estimate).

alternatives.why_not: equally capable; for a team of 8 with a DevOps engineer (team.has_devops=true), ready-made GitHub deploy actions for AWS ECS on Fargate mean less pipeline code to maintain

tradeoffs: Secrets must be stored as encrypted environment secrets

supporting.choice: Amazon CloudWatch in ap-south-1 (Mumbai) (logs, metrics, alarms)
supporting.justification: The 300 ms p95 target and the 99.95% availability target are watched by latency and error-rate alerts; logs and metrics stay with AWS in ap-south-1 (Mumbai), so there is no second vendor.

alternatives.why_not: stores data only in the US or EU

tradeoffs: Log retention costs grow with traffic

supporting.choice: Double-entry ledger module (append-only journal, SERIALIZABLE transactions, idempotency keys)
supporting.justification: Loan disbursals and EMI collections post balanced debit/credit entries that are never updated in place; reconciliation compares the ledger with gateway settlement reports.

alternatives.why_not: no audit trail and race conditions

tradeoffs: Corrections are reversing entries, not edits

supporting.choice: KYC document vault (private encrypted bucket) + regulated KYC verification partner
supporting.justification: KYC uploads are stored encrypted with access logging and retention rules; identity checks go through a licensed verification partner chosen by the business.

alternatives.choice: Storing KYC files in the app database
alternatives.why_not: large blobs and broader access

tradeoffs: Verification partner contract and API not selected here

supporting.choice: AWS WAF + AWS KMS + AWS Secrets Manager + AWS CloudTrail
supporting.justification: Taking payments with priorities.security=5 and compliance=iso27001,pci_dss needs protection in front of the app and control of keys, secrets and audit evidence: AWS WAF in front of the load balancer or CloudFront (managed rule sets plus rate limits on login and payment routes), AWS KMS customer-managed keys for the database, bucket and backup encryption, AWS Secrets Manager for database and gateway credentials, and AWS CloudTrail for an audit trail of API and console actions kept in a write-protected bucket in ap-south-1 (Mumbai). These are the building blocks an assessor asks to see; they do not make the system compliant on their own. The cost line is a planning estimate (provider list prices for these services were not read), driven mainly by request volume.

alternatives.why_not: a second vendor in front of the AWS footprint; AWS WAF keeps rules, keys and logs in one account

tradeoffs: Rule tuning is ongoing work: start WAF rules in count mode, then block
Key and secret rotation must be scheduled and tested

assumptions: Hosting AWS ECS on Fargate (+ Application Load Balancer): $200-900/month at the 'medium' tier.
Database Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL 17: $270-1400/month (HA doubles instances).
Availability ≥99.95%: a second app instance in another zone $200-900/month (the hosting line counted again).

auth: Amazon Cognito user pool + Amazon SNS SMS OTP in ap-south-1 (Mumbai) $440-1595/month. Cognito Lite: 10,000 MAU free, then a flat $0.0055 per MAU at every volume (Amazon Cognito pricing; the knowledge base holds no volume-tier table, so a tier discount, if any, is not modelled). MAU is taken as 30%-100% of ~300,000 users = 90,000-300,000 MAU (planning heuristic), so the lower bound is max(0, 90,000 - 10,000) x $0.0055 and the upper bound max(0, 300,000 - 10,000) x $0.0055; SMS is counted once, in the Phone OTP line.
storage: Amazon S3 (ap-south-1 (Mumbai)) $0/month here: the files it holds are priced by volume in the 'Stored data' line, not charged twice.
cache: Amazon ElastiCache for Valkey in ap-south-1 (Mumbai) $50-300/month.
ml: Separate Python inference service (FastAPI + ONNX Runtime) in the same private network $40-200/month.
observability: Amazon CloudWatch in ap-south-1 (Mumbai) (logs, metrics, alarms) $30-200/month.
other: AWS WAF + AWS KMS + AWS Secrets Manager + AWS CloudTrail $40-200/month.

Stored data (object storage: files and media) ~500 GB after 12 months at ~$0.02-0.035/GB-month: $10-19/month (year-end volume used as an upper bound, not an average); this is the only charge for these files (the storage service's own line adds nothing on top), and database rows are assumed small.

Phone OTP: 300,000 users x 0.3-1.0 OTP logins/month at Amazon SNS SMS at $0.004 (AWS SMS price list, 11 Nov 2026), x1 at the lower bound and x1.5 at the upper bound (retries and DLT rejections, planning heuristic): $360-1800/month (long-lived sessions keep OTPs rare).
Spiky traffic: the upper bound is a peak month; with autoscaling, quiet months run near the lower bound.
Excluded: payment gateway fees (~2% per transaction) are a share of revenue, not infrastructure.
Excluded: taxes, domain names, paid support plans and data-egress spikes. Order-of-magnitude band, not a quote.

warnings.message: Every launch user (10,000) is assumed online at once at peak; sizing uses this conservative figure.

DPDP Act 2023: collect consent with a clear notice, support access/correction/erasure requests, keep a breach runbook (the DPDP Rules 2025 require prompt intimation to the Board and affected people, then a detailed report within 72 hours; the Rules commence in phases, so confirm which apply on your launch date) and delete data when the purpose ends. Hosting in India simplifies transfers; legal review still required.
ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certifies your organisation's ISMS, not a cloud provider's badge: keep asset inventory, access reviews, logging and change management for this system.

PCI DSS v4.0.1: card data handled only by the gateway's hosted checkout or embedded payment form keeps scope small and can qualify for SAQ A; with an embedded form the page must also be protected from script attacks (Requirements 6.4.3/11.6.1, or the processor's confirmation), and your acquirer confirms which SAQ applies.

RBI storage of payment system data: payment system operators and the gateways and vendors in their chain store the end-to-end payment data only in India; data processed abroad must be deleted there and brought back within one business day or 24 hours, whichever is earlier.

Upper estimate $7684/month is 28% above the $6000 budget at peak usage; the largest upper-bound items are Phone OTP SMS fees (up to $1,800) and Amazon Cognito monthly-active-user charges (up to $1,595). Launch near the $1660 lower bound and set billing alerts at the budget.

assumptions: Knowledge base as of 2026-11-11; lifecycle and pricing judgements use that date, not the run date.
Scale tier 'medium' from 300,000 users and ~10,000 peak concurrent users (people, not requests per second; used only for sizing and cost).
